summary: Planner 30-minute wake job: keep and automate every hand-caught gap, retire only when wakes find nothing

options.description: Keep the wake; every hand-caught gap becomes an automation task; retire the job only when consecutive wakes find nothing
Keep the wake as a standing manual check with no automation obligation
Delete the wake job now and rely on the dispatch tick and route-to-planner

body: Operator ruling 2026-11-08 (decision rubric). Problem: the 30-minute planner wake (operator order 2026-11-06) catches landing gaps by hand (stale executors, unarmed PRs, unqueued filings, dead panes). Options weighed: keep the wake as a standing manual check; keep it and turn every gap it catches into an automation task until a wake finds nothing, then retire the job; retire it now and rely on the dispatch tick. Counter-argument to keep-and-automate: each automation task costs budget in a tight window; it survives because every gap caught so far recurred (AISDLC-1242, 1243, 1244, 1245, 1246 are the first batch).
